tasks.short: Arrange appointments for lawyers, checking availability, urgency and confidentiality.

steps.what: Read the appointment request and clarify participants, purpose, duration and constraints.
Check calendars, travel buffers and room availability for suitable slots.
Exchange proposed times and resolve clashes, urgency or sensitive attendance.
Create the appointment and send invitations with appropriate visibility and meeting details.
Check acceptances and chase missing confirmations.

tasks.design: Configure structured requests, availability rules, booking links and neutral reminders in the {WORKFLOW} and {CALENDAR}. The legal assistant resolves difficult clashes and checks recipients and visibility before invitations leave the {CALENDAR}; acceptance tracking removes routine chasing through the {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests arrived in different formats, and booking rules were implicit. External availability and sensitive participant lists still required coordination.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing booking features cover routine coordination. AI-assisted coding can make small adapters and request forms cheaper to build where configuration falls short.
tasks.still_hard: Urgent legal appointments, external calendars and confidential attendance require context. Court-fixed dates cannot be moved through ordinary booking rules.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising which clash merits interrupting a lawyer and negotiating without exposing confidential information.

ambition.what: Self-service appointment requests for regional office staff

tasks.altitude: The week shifts toward urgent clashes and preparation gaps. With delegated authority, the assistant can release routine appointments within agreed scheduling priorities; lawyers retain substantive priority decisions.

reach.task: Coordinate shared executive and legal meeting availability
reach.learn: Calendar delegation, travel buffers and escalation priorities

evidence.claim: Existing calendar booking rules and reminders can handle routine appointments without a model.
Microsoft 365 Copilot can turn an email thread into an invitation with an agenda.
The UK department evaluation reported scheduling taking longer on average; automation needs a local comparison.
EU AI Act requirements depend on use; routine scheduling differs from allocating tasks or monitoring staff.

assumptions: The setting is an internal legal team in a company with 200 to 2,000 staff.
Structured intake covers routine requests; unusual requests remain with the assistant.
Routine reminders contain neutral appointment details and follow agreed rules.
The coordination prior is useful, but this reconstruction places more work in the mailbox than its weak mail estimate.
Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
Access work includes GDPR review and employee consultation where national rules apply.
unknowns: Which booking, availability and delegation features the existing {CALENDAR} supports
Whether assistants may release routine appointments without lawyer approval
How many appointments involve court-fixed dates or confidential participant lists
Whether national rules require consultation for changed calendar access
research_questions: Do booking links reduce coordination time for external participants?
Which invitation fields need a human check to prevent confidentiality errors?
Does structured intake reduce clarification without discouraging urgent requests?
new_work: Maintain appointment types, buffers and visibility rules.
Handle booking failures and unresolved clashes.
Review invitation recipients and confidential details.
Check reminder effectiveness and excessive notifications.

tasks.short: Draft, format and circulate office memos from lawyers’ instructions.

steps.what: Receive instructions and clarify the memo’s audience, purpose and required action.
Find supporting records and the current approved memo template.
Draft the memo and apply the required formatting.

loop.input: Memo brief, approved template and permission-checked source pack
loop.output: Memo draft with source references and marked gaps
loop.check: Validate required fields and source links; the assistant checks factual support, recipients and wording.
loop.stop: One draft and at most one revision against explicit corrections; incomplete or unsupported drafts return to manual drafting.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle fixed notices, but narrative instructions require wording and synthesis. Invoke the loop only for those passages.

steps.what: Review the memo’s substance and approve its final wording and audience.
Circulate the approved version and save the distribution record.

tasks.design: A structured brief in the {WORKFLOW} retrieves approved sources and templates from the {DOCS}. A deterministic generator fills standard notices, while a bounded drafting loop handles narrative passages; lawyer approval unlocks distribution through the {EMAIL} and saves the approved version in the {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Templates covered formatting but could not turn varied instructions into clear prose. Source selection, version control and approval often depended on mailbox exchanges.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded drafting can produce a reviewable first version from supplied sources. AI-assisted coding lowers the effort of connecting templates, source records and approval states.
tasks.still_hard: Ambiguous instructions and legal implications still need clarification. Drafting may save little time when reviewers must substantially rewrite the result.
tasks.human_edge: Understanding what readers should do and detecting wording that changes a legal or organisational commitment.

ambition.what: Plain-language action briefs for non-legal managers

tasks.altitude: The assistant spends more time clarifying instructions and improving reader comprehension. They can choose approved formats and distribution timing within delegated limits; lawyers retain approval of substance.

reach.task: Translate approved office policy into practical staff instructions
reach.learn: Audience testing, policy implementation and accessible writing

evidence.claim: Templates and structured records can generate routine memos deterministically.
The UK department evaluation found drafting time savings but also hallucinations and no demonstrated overall productivity increase.
Dutch professional guidance recommends protecting confidential information and manually verifying legal citations.
The EU AI Act includes an AI literacy requirement.

assumptions: Routine memos use approved templates and identifiable supporting records.
Only authorised confidential material enters the drafting environment; GDPR applies.
The high automation prior applies mainly to drafting and formatting, while substantive approval remains human.
The new action-brief service would need lawyer approval and an agreed audience.
Time shares include the lawyer handoff and are planning estimates, as are build ranges.
Access work includes information-security review and employee consultation where national rules apply.
unknowns: The proportion of fixed notices versus narrative memos
Who has authority to approve each memo category
Whether source records have reliable permissions and version identifiers
Which national confidentiality and employee-consultation rules apply
research_questions: How often can a template produce the complete memo without a model?
Does source-linked drafting reduce total drafting and review time?
Can office staff correctly identify required actions from the approved memo?
new_work: Review generated wording against its sources.
Maintain templates, approved phrases and distribution groups.
Resolve incomplete briefs and conflicting source versions.
Maintain drafting checks and investigate unsupported statements.

tasks.short: Package search findings and obtain a lawyer’s approval before using them.

steps.what: Collect articles and search results relevant to the lawyer’s research request.
Check citations, jurisdiction, publication dates and source versions in the legal research service.
Select relevant passages and annotate how each source addresses the request.

loop.input: Research request and verified source texts
loop.output: Proposed relevance labels, exact excerpts and source locations
loop.check: Match excerpts exactly to source text; the assistant checks relevance, context and omitted qualifications.
loop.stop: One pass per source within the configured document limit; unreadable or oversized sources return to manual annotation.
loop.why_not_simpler: Metadata filters cannot establish whether a passage addresses a free-text legal question.

steps.what: Assemble findings, source copies and unresolved questions into a review packet.
Assess the findings and approve which sources may support the legal work.
Record the approval and share the approved packet with the matter team.

tasks.design: An adapter imports selected results from the legal research service in the {OTHER} into a permission-controlled source register in the {DOCS}. After manual citation checks, a bounded loop proposes exact excerpts and relevance labels, and a deterministic generator assembles the review packet; the {WORKFLOW} records lawyer approval before internal sharing through the {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sources, annotations and approvals were separated across files and messages. Legal relevance could not be reduced to metadata, and licensing limited reusable integrations.
tasks.enabler_now: Small adapters and packet generators are cheaper to build. Bounded text classification can help triage supplied sources while retaining exact evidence for review.
tasks.still_hard: Current legal authority, jurisdiction and source licensing need careful checks. A relevant excerpt can mislead when its surrounding qualifications are omitted.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising weak authority, contradictory sources and when the research question needs a lawyer’s clarification.

ambition.what: Source-update alerts for previously approved research packets

tasks.altitude: The assistant spends less time assembling packets and more time checking source quality and unresolved questions. They can manage packet completeness and update alerts; lawyers retain decisions about legal reliance.

reach.task: Prepare traceable evidence packs for operational recommendations
reach.learn: Source evaluation, evidence registers and separating findings from recommendations

evidence.claim: Source registers, exact-text checks and review-packet generation can use deterministic code.
Dutch professional guidance recommends manually verifying legal citations and protecting confidential information.
In the Netherlands, statutory lawyer secrecy extends to employees and staff.
The supplied digest contains no documented case establishing savings for this legal research submission task.

assumptions: The {OTHER} category is a legal research service.
This task packages findings from searches; full legal research and legal advice remain separate work.
Imports are limited to sources permitted by licence and access rights.
The prior for external action is rejected here: submission and approval normally occur inside the legal team.
The high judgement prior supports retaining citation checks and lawyer approval.
Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
GDPR applies; confidentiality and employee consultation also depend on national rules.
Source-update alerts initially cover version changes detectable through permitted metadata.
unknowns: Which legal research services permit export, integration and model processing
Which jurisdictions and source types the legal team uses
How findings and approvals are recorded today
Whether approved sources expose reliable update metadata
Which national professional-secrecy and consultation rules apply
research_questions: Can exact-text matching reliably identify excerpt locations across the permitted source formats?
Do proposed relevance labels reduce total annotation and review time?
Which source changes merit an alert instead of creating noise?
new_work: Check proposed excerpts for context and omitted qualifications.
Maintain source identifiers, permissions and import adapters.
Resolve unreadable documents and conflicting versions.
Triage source-update alerts and request renewed lawyer review when needed.

tasks.short: Arrange lawyers’ travel, obtain approval and provide a usable itinerary.

steps.what: Clarify destinations, appointment times, traveller preferences and spending limits.
Search the travel booking service for transport and accommodation options.
Compare total costs, arrival buffers and cancellation terms in a proposed itinerary.
Approve the itinerary, spending limit and any policy exception.
Check current prices and terms, then purchase the approved travel.
Send the final itinerary, add calendar entries and forward the invoice to finance.

tasks.design: A travel request in the {WORKFLOW} draws appointment details from the {CALENDAR} and applies configured filters in the travel booking service in the {OTHER}. A deterministic generator builds the comparison and itinerary; after spend approval, the assistant confirms the purchase, and an integration distributes booking details through the {EMAIL}, {CALENDAR} and {ERP}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Traveller preferences and approval limits lived in messages. Changing fares, cancellation terms and fragmented booking interfaces made dependable purchasing automation expensive.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured requests, existing travel filters and small itinerary generators cover much of the preparation. AI-assisted coding reduces the cost of linking booking confirmations to calendars and invoice intake.
tasks.still_hard: Live prices, disruptions and cancellation conditions remain variable. Purchasing stays manual where the service lacks a dependable interface or the approved option has changed.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing a workable journey around demanding appointments and resolving disruptions with the traveller.

ambition.what: Pre-departure arrival-buffer checks for legal travel

tasks.altitude: The assistant spends more time on workable journeys and disruption handling. With delegated limits, they can choose equivalent alternatives within an approved budget; larger changes still return to the approver.

reach.learn: Fare conditions, realistic connection buffers and disruption recovery

reach.task: Improve travel policy using recurring exception patterns
reach.learn: Approval design, total trip cost and supplier-service assessment

evidence.claim: Structured requests, configured policy filters and itinerary generation can reduce travel preparation without an autonomous agent.
Live booking remains difficult to automate when prices, terms or interfaces cannot be checked reliably.
The supplied digest contains no travel-booking product evidence or documented legal-travel case.

assumptions: The {OTHER} category is a travel booking service.
Its existing filters cover common destinations, dates and policy limits.
Comparison uses structured prices and fare conditions; ambiguous conditions receive human review.
The lawyer is the traveller and has spending authority; otherwise the approval role must change.
The assistant checks the final purchase against approval and escalates material changes.
Invoice submission does not approve or release payment.
The coordination prior is retained, but external purchasing remains human without a proven interface.
Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
GDPR applies to traveller details; access and employee consultation follow applicable national rules.
unknowns: Which filtering and export features the travel booking service supports
Who approves spending and policy exceptions
Whether booking confirmations have dependable structured fields
How often travel changes after approval
Whether delegated authority covers equivalent replacement journeys
research_questions: Do structured requests reduce clarification and rejected itineraries?
Can total trip costs and cancellation terms be compared without free-text interpretation?
Do pre-departure buffer checks identify actionable problems early enough?
new_work: Maintain traveller preferences, policy limits and approval routes.
Check changing fares and terms before purchase.
Resolve failed confirmation imports and unmatched invoices.
Review arrival-buffer alerts and handle travel disruptions.

role.altitude: The week shifts from repeated coordination, formatting and packet assembly toward confidentiality checks, source quality and difficult exceptions. Delegated rights can expand to routine scheduling and travel alternatives within approved limits; lawyers retain legal judgement, substantive approval and decisions about reliance.
reach: Coordinate executive and legal calendars with the executive administrative assistant.
Help the administrative services manager improve travel and office-policy processes.
Build traceable evidence packs with the management analyst.
skills_to_grow: Confidentiality, permissions and GDPR-aware information handling
Source verification and document version control
Calendar delegation and travel exception handling
Evaluating total preparation and review time
role.ambitious_version: Provide a shared legal coordination service for regional offices, with self-service appointment intake, plain-language action briefs, research-source update alerts and pre-departure travel checks. Start with reusable templates and configuration, then connect authorised records; wider decision rights require explicit delegation.
